name: Lau mam
summary: A fermented-fish hotpot the provincial tourism center still describes as a Long An specialty. At least three mắm go in the broth: mắm sặc, mắm trèn, and mắm linh. Eat it with fresh rice noodles and a large plate of greens, dipped in and taken out while they are still crisp. Not lunch at the Holy See. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: The article says miền Tây in general and Long An in particular. Resolution 202/2025/QH15 joined that province into Tây Ninh. The homepage had already grouped lẩu mắm with the old Long An goods.
taste: The broth is gently sweet, not the fatty sweetness of a bone broth, brown from the mắm, and thick from pounded garlic and chili with lemongrass. The center says the Long An pot is kept from being too salty. It also says the smell is strong if you are not used to it.
The three pastes are mắm sặc for the smell, mắm trèn for a deep sweetness and a dark color, and mắm linh for the fat of field fish.
howToEat: Share the pot with fresh rice noodles. Dip the greens and take them out while they are still crisp. The article says three or four large plates of greens: bông súng, đọt nhãn lồng, ngò gai, ngò om, cải xanh, rau muống, đậu rồng, rau đắng, rau càng cua, bông so đũa, cà phổi, bắp chuối, ớt hiểm, tỏi, and especially ngọn rau dừa. Okra and straw mushrooms go in when the pot boils.
The pot can hold seafood, beef, and pork, and field fish just cooked: eel, cá rô, cá sặc rằn, cá dầy, and snakehead, with mắm sặc. A price is Check on arrival. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: The article does not name a street in the new province. It still sends you to Long An. Check on arrival for a door.

seoDescription: Fermented-fish hotpot with mắm sặc, mắm trèn, and mắm linh, fresh noodles, and a large plate of greens. The article still says Long An. A price is Check on arrival.
